intended_object: The set of points of a coordinate line ("dimension") in the plane K×K given by two points `zero` and `one`, i.e. the affine line {zero + t·(one − zero) : t ∈ K}. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: `points L` is the range of `L.pt`, and `L.pt t = L.zero + t·(L.one − L.zero)` coordinate by coordinate. So it is exactly the parametrised line through `zero` and `one`. Over any commutative ring this set equals Mathlib's `line[K, zero, one] = affineSpan K {zero, one}`, since the vector span of the two points is `K ∙ (one − zero)`. When `zero = one` it is the single point, which matches the affine span. The construction would also make sense in any K-module. But `Dim` is defined with points in `K × K`, and the rest of this planar development needs the plane: `cross`, `side` and the figures use 2D determinants. So this accessor is stated at its natural generality inside the library's own setting.
